jobs.title: Junior Cyber Security Analyst
jobs.description:
This is a Fully Remote Job

About Our Client:

The organization operates within the cybersecurity field, addressing the challenge of protecting systems, applications, networks, and data from evolving cyber threats. It focuses on maintaining high security standards by monitoring, investigating, and responding to security incidents, as well as improving security controls.

About the Opportunity:

The JUNIOR CYBER SECURITY ANALYST role is designed to support the security team in safeguarding the company's digital infrastructure. This position is responsible for monitoring security alerts, analyzing threats, responding to incidents, and assisting in the implementation of security measures. The role contributes to maintaining the organization's security posture and compliance with relevant standards.

Responsibilities:

Monitor networks using SIEM, EDR, NDR, and DLP technologies for security issues.
Respond to email security incidents and reports.
Investigate security breaches and cybersecurity incidents.
Install and operate security software to protect systems.
Document security incidents and assess their impact.
Conduct tests to identify network vulnerabilities.
Remediate detected vulnerabilities.
Stay informed on IT security trends.
Research and recommend security enhancements.
Ensure systems are updated and assist in patching.
Perform initial triage of security alerts.
Monitor security reports and dashboards.
Participate in audits and procure necessary artifacts.
Create incident reports for findings beyond alerts.
Handle time-sensitive compliance tasks including reviews and training.

jobs.description:
Position: OT Security Analyst

Location: Dallas TX***Onsite***

Duration: 1 Years

Oversee SOC operations during assigned shifts, ensuring efficient workflow, proper escalation procedures, adherence to SLAs, and effective communication between analysts.
Lead investigations and response to complex security incidents impacting OT systems, networks, and applications. This includes coordinating efforts with other teams and business units (e.g. Networking, Architecture, CIP Compliance).
Perform in-depth analysis of security alerts and logs common in ICS/SCADA systems to identify indicators of compromise (IOCs).
Make real-time decisions on incident severity, containment strategies, and escalation paths and actions taken by Tier 1 & 2 analysts for incidents.
Evaluate and provide feedback on the performance of security technologies (e.g. SIEM, SOAR, IIDS/IPS) used in the SOC. Identify and oversee the optimization of detection rules to reduce false positives.
Develop, test, and implement custom detection rules, correlation searches, baseline drift and use cases within the toolset to improve threat detection capabilities specifically tailored to OT protocols and environments.
Proactively search for IOCs and misconfigurations within the OT environment using threat intelligence, anomaly detection techniques, and knowledge of attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) relevant to ICS/SCADA systems.
Create, maintain, and refine incident response playbooks, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and runbooks based on lessons learned from incidents, threat intelligence, and industry best practices.
Ensure all actions, findings, and decisions made during incident handling are thoroughly documented in the SOC's ticketing system. Prepare clear and concise reports for management on security incidents and trends.
Provide guidance, training, and mentorship to Tier 1 & 2 analysts on incident handling, analysis techniques, tools, and OT security concepts.
Participate in training sessions and simulations to stay current on cyber threats, OT security best practices, and monitoring tools.
Stay current on NERC-CIP standards (specifically 2/3), NIST CSF, Purdue Model for Industrial Control Systems, ISO 27001 frameworks, and other relevant OT security regulations.

Education, Experience, & Skill Requirements

Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field required. Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 5-7 years of experience in a cybersecurity-focused role; SOC experience strongly preferred.
3+ years of direct experience working with Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control Systems (ICS) environments including hands-on knowledge of SCADA systems, PLCs, RTUs, HMIs, and industrial networks.
Advanced certifications strongly desired. Examples include: CySA+, CEH, OSCP, GICSP, CCNA Security, or relevant OT security certifications (e.g., ISA/IEC 62443).
Deep understanding of cybersecurity fundamentals such as networking protocols (TCP/IP, UDP, DNS), operating systems (Windows, Linux), and security architecture principles.
Strong knowledge of OT Protocols such as DNP3, Modbus, IEC 104, OPC UA, including packet analysis and understanding protocol vulnerabilities.
Experienced with Security Technologies such as SIEM, SOAR, IIDS/IPS, endpoint detection solutions, network traffic analysis tools.
Exceptional analytical mindset and attention to detail. Ability to analyze complex data sets, identify patterns, and draw meaningful conclusions.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills to effectively communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to create clear and concise reports.
Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor junior analysts.
Ability to work in a 24/7 shift-based SOC environment, including covering for teammates and occasional after-hours support.

Measures of Success

Demonstrates leadership in handling complex security incidents and coordinating response efforts.
Significant improvement in key performance indicators (e.g., reduction in mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to respond (MTTR), false positive rate).
Successful development and implementation of new detection rules and use cases that improve threat coverage.
Ensures Oncor's timelines, budgets, and deliverable objectives are met.
Ensures the DGM SOC's SLAs are met or exceeded.
Works closely with multiple business units to improve cross-functional communication and efficiencies.
Demonstrates skills in prioritization and multi-tasking, and success in adapting to change in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrates ability to interface with internal and external business partners in a professional manner.

Monitor and manage MMS’ daily cash position, make recommendations on Investments and quarter-back this process to reduce cost of cash

Duration: 8 Months

Agency: OIT

Job ID: 167325

Work Location: 100% Remote unless they reside in Maine. If they reside in Maine, they will need to report onsite one day bi-weekly, and travel costs to State office locations will not be reimbursed. (Will only consider candidates in the Eastern and Central time zones) Job Description:

The Application Security Program Manager (Business SME 1) supports the Information Security Office in transitioning the State's secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) from a near-complete modernization project to a sustained operating program. The position coordinates the people, decisions, workflows, and measures needed to make application security practices workable across State technology teams. As initial transition tasks are completed, the manager shifts effort to adoption, performance, risk reduction, and continuous improvement across the broader application security portfolio. This is a cross-functional program management role. The manager works with Vulnerability Management, Security Architecture, Governance Risk and Compliance (GRC), Application Development, GitHub Governance, infrastructure and platform teams, agency product owners, and vendors. The manager drives follow-through, program adoption, and accountability across stakeholders and elevates decisions to the appropriate owner; specialist teams retain their established technical, product, and risk approval authority. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
The manager in this role requires the ability to oversee application security efforts across multiple teams and drive program improvements to strengthen the State of Maine's security posture. We seek a self-motivated individual who thrives in fast-paced environments, seamlessly drives initiatives with multiple stakeholders, and has demonstrable experience in application security leadership. The candidate must have 8 to 10 years of experience in leadership roles, program management, and change agent roles, improving application security program maturity. The selected candidate will be required to pass the required background checks as a condition of employment.

About The Role

The Sales Operations Analyst transforms data into insights, recommendations, and scalable solutions that improve sales performance and operational effectiveness.

This role goes beyond reporting. You will define business problems, identify root causes, evaluate solutions, recommend actions, and help implement repeatable business playbooks. You will partner with Sales Leadership, Finance, HR, Compensation, IT, and other teams to support territory management, quota processes, performance reporting, account alignment, data governance, and process improvement.

Process Improvement & Playbooks

Develop scalable solutions that reduce manual effort and improve consistency.
Translate one-time fixes into sustainable business practices.

Utilize AI tools responsibly to increase analytical efficiency and operational effectiveness.

Demonstrated ability to use data to solve business problems and support decision-making.

Strong Excel skills and experience working with complex datasets.
Ability to investigate data issues, determine root causes, and recommend solutions.
Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.

You enjoy solving complex business problems, learning new technologies, and working in a fast-paced environment where priorities evolve. You are naturally curious, challenge assumptions, and have the ability to move from analysis to action.

Deliver accurate, actionable reporting and insights.
Recommend practical actions that improve business outcomes.
Build playbooks and scalable solutions that drive consistency and efficiency.
Address root causes instead of repeatedly solving symptoms.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Project Manager - Enterprise Merchandise

As a Project Manager, you will be the operational backbone of our enterprise sales process. You will partner directly with Account Executives to manage the complete order-to-delivery lifecycle for clients, ensuring flawless execution and exceptional customer experience. Working alongside the sales team, you will leverage deep product knowledge and operational excellence to support deal closure and drive client satisfaction. Your role is critical to scaling our enterprise business while maintaining the quality and attention to detail that defines Quince.

Responsibilities

Assume deal ownership post-sale, from logo approval through invoicing, delivery and issue resolution
Track and update all project progress in our B2B operations tracker, sharing timely updates with clients and Account Executives; communicate with clarity even when information is incomplete or ambiguous
Finalize customization details, communicate delivery timelines, and manage approval workflows with clients and internal teams
Field and resolve client support requests including sample returns, shipping and tracking, troubleshooting missing or damaged items, and expediting requests when possible
Demonstrate strategic thinking by proactively identifying opportunities to streamline operations, reduce tasks, and propose solutions that enhance client experience
Over-communicate with customers on all issues, managing them with confidence and compassion; reply to requests with urgency and follow through on every commitment made

Qualifications

Required:

Familiarity with CRM or project management platforms to track client data, order status, and communication history (Hubspot preferred)
Proficiency in Google Workspace
Experience managing internal and external stakeholders with distinct approaches
Self-starter comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
Extremely detail-oriented with ability to operate with a sense of urgency
Customer service oriented and customer obsessed—committed to exceeding expectations at every touchpoint

Customer experience or customer-facing background (email-based support, retail customer service, or account coordination)
Exposure to apparel, decoration, manufacturing, or promotional products industry

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

What We Do

At Applegreen, our mission is to delight customers in transit with passionate hospitality and brands they love.
Applegreen is a leading roadside retailer operating high-quality travel plazas and service areas in the US, Ireland, and the UK. Founded on a commitment to innovation, operational excellence, and customer experience, Applegreen combines fuel, convenience retail, and a diverse portfolio of food and beverage offerings to create welcoming destinations for customers.
In the U.S., Applegreen partners with major transportation authorities and operates more than 120 service plazas along some of the country’s busiest highways and turnpikes. The company is known for modern facilities, strong national and local food brands, and an emphasis on freshness, quality, and sustainability.
At Applegreen, our people are at the heart of what we do. We foster a culture that values teamwork, development, and accountability, offering employees opportunities to grow their careers in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Applegreen continues to expand while remaining focused on delivering exceptional service to customers and creating a great place to work.

Our Core Value

Our core values define who we are and guide how we work every day. They shape our decisions, inspire our actions, and influence how we engage with our customers, suppliers, business partners, and one another.
Our customers and communities are at the heart of everything we do.
We value and develop our people.
We are driven by pace, passion and performance.
We seek opportunities and embrace change.

Benefits You Receive

Applegreen offers a competitive benefits package designed to support the health and financial well-being of our associates and families. Available benefits include a variety of company-sponsored and voluntary options such as:
Medical/Dental/Vision Insurance
Paid Time Off
401 (k) with Company Match
10% Annual Bonus
Earned Wage Access – Pay on Demand
Education Assistance
Employee Referral Bonus
Pet Insurance

POSITION SUMMARY

Applegreen is seeking a Project Manager - Capital Projects to support the execution of its U.S. capital investment program across the travel plaza portfolio. Reporting to the Director, U.S. Capital Projects, this position will manage multiple concurrent capital projects from initial planning and design through construction, turnover, and opening.
The portfolio includes QSR and retail remodels, brand conversions, new concept fit-outs, refresh/reimage programs, retail renovations, and other strategic capital improvements across active travel plaza environments. The Project Manager will work closely with internal Operations, Commercial, Finance, Procurement, and other business teams, as well as restaurant and retail brand partners, architects, engineers, general contractors, vendors, and consultants.
This is a hands-on project management role requiring strong ownership, organization, sound judgment, and the ability to manage numerous projects simultaneously across multiple markets. Success in the role requires delivering projects safely, on schedule, within approved capital budgets, to applicable brand and quality standards, and with minimal disruption to ongoing operations and sales.

Key Responsibilities

• Manage multiple concurrent capital projects through the full project lifecycle, including scope development, design, budgeting, procurement, permitting, construction, turnover, and closeout.
• Develop and maintain project budgets, schedules, forecasts, milestone tracking, and status reporting; proactively identify and communicate risks to cost, schedule, quality, and operations.
• Coordinate architects, engineers, consultants, general contractors, vendors, equipment suppliers, and brand partners to drive projects from concept through opening.
• Partner closely with Operations and Commercial teams to align project execution with operational requirements, merchandising strategies, customer experience, and business objectives.
• Manage QSR and retail new fit-outs, remodels, brand conversions, reimages, refreshes, and renovations within active travel plaza environments.
• Develop project phasing and execution strategies designed to minimize operational downtime, disruption to customers, and lost sales.
• Review construction drawings, specifications, proposals, scopes of work, and quantities for completeness, constructability, coordination, and alignment with project objectives.
• Support contractor bidding, scope leveling, procurement coordination, contract administration, change-order review, and project cost control.
• Lead project meetings and conduct regular site visits to monitor construction progress, quality, safety, schedule, and coordination among trades and stakeholders.
• Resolve field conditions, technical issues, scope conflicts, and other project challenges in a timely manner, escalating material risks with recommended solutions when appropriate.
• Coordinate with restaurant and retail brands to ensure projects meet applicable brand standards, equipment requirements, operational criteria, and opening requirements.
• Maintain accurate project documentation, including budgets, schedules, contracts, change orders, meeting minutes, risk logs, punch lists, and closeout documentation.
• Provide clear and timely project reporting to the Director, U.S. Capital Projects and other senior stakeholders.
• Manage turnover and opening activities in coordination with Operations, Commercial, IT, Procurement, vendors, and brand partners.
• Identify opportunities to improve project delivery processes, standardization, cost efficiency, schedule performance, and execution across the broader capital portfolio.

Education, Qualifications & Experience

• Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant project management experience will be considered.
• 5+ years of project management experience in construction, development, retail, restaurant/QSR, hospitality, convenience retail, or a related multi-site environment preferred.
• Demonstrated experience independently managing multiple concurrent construction or capital projects.
• Strong understanding of project budgeting, scheduling, procurement, construction documentation, change management, and project closeout.
• Experience working in active operating environments and managing construction while minimizing disruption to the business strongly preferred.
• QSR, restaurant, convenience retail, travel plaza, hospitality, or other multi-site consumer experience preferred.
• Experience coordinating with general contractors, architects, engineers, vendors, and external brand partners.
• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel; experience with project management, scheduling, and reporting platforms preferred (Procore, Smartsheet).
• Ability and willingness to travel regularly to project locations and adjust work hours when project execution requires it.

Job Description

Leverage your deep technical expertise and leadership to guide cutting-edge projects, fostering growth and innovation in a dynamic environment.

As an AI Transformation Lead Technical Program Manager at JPMorgan Chase in the Corporate Sector- Employee Platforms, you will drive the successful delivery of complex technology projects and programs that will help reaching business goals across the firm. You will lead strategy-to-execution for an Operating Committee-sponsored, multi-year transformation spanning HR and Technology. You will translate executive intent into a clear outcomes framework, integrated roadmap, and disciplined delivery across multiple workstreams. You'll partner closely with engineering, architecture, product, HR, and control functions to drive delivery transparency, manage interdependencies, and enable sustained adoption—while embedding responsible AI capabilities into program execution.

Job Responsibilities

Own end-to-end program delivery for a complex, multi-year transformation, translating Operating Committee priorities into clear problem statements, target outcomes, milestones, and measurable success metrics.
Lead governance and executive operating cadence, including OKRs/KPIs, executive steering materials, RAID, dependency management, delivery health reporting, and decision/approval forums to enable timely, well-informed decisions.
Create and maintain integrated program plans across teams and vendors, including sequencing, resourcing inputs, requirements/feature tracking, milestones, and cutover/rollout planning to ensure on-time delivery and seamless integration with existing platforms.
Drive cross-functional alignment with engineering, architecture, product, HR, and key stakeholders to clarify scope, value case, dependencies, and trade-offs; maintain accountability across workstreams and remove blockers.
Enable change management, adoption, and benefits realization, partnering with HR and change stakeholders on communications, training approaches, readiness tracking, and measurement of realized outcomes to ensure solutions embed into business-as-usual.
Proactively manage risks, issues, and dependencies, surfacing concerns early, driving mitigation plans, and executing appropriate escalation paths with clear options and recommendations.
Deliver executive-ready narratives and insights, using crisp synthesis and data visualization to communicate progress, risks, trade-offs, decisions required, and recommendations.
Facilitate workshops and decision forums that build shared understanding, resolve ambiguity, and maintain momentum across HR and Technology leadership.
Strengthen delivery discipline and continuous improvement, applying modern delivery practices and helping teams inspect/adapt operating rhythms, metrics, and ways of working to improve predictability and outcomes.
Champion AI fluency and responsible adoption of agentic capabilities, identifying and delivering opportunities to embed AI-assisted workflows into program execution (e.g., portfolio insights, delivery automation, risk identification, stakeholder communications) in partnership with product, engineering, and control stakeholders.
Lead experimentation and learning loops, running lightweight pilots with defined success measures, capturing lessons learned, and scaling what works with appropriate governance and risk management.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

5+ years of experience or equivalent expertise in technical program management, leading complex technology projects and programs in a large organization
Demonstrated ability to lead delivery across multiple teams and stakeholder groups, including complex planning, dependency management, and executive-level communication.
Strong strategic and analytical capability to define success measures, assess performance, identify improvement opportunities, and drive data-driven metrics (OKRs/KPIs, delivery health indicators).
Strong governance and controls orientation, including risk/issue management, documentation rigor, and operating committee/steering engagement.
Proven ability to deliver adoption and change outcomes (communications, readiness, training coordination, benefits tracking) as part of sustained transformation.
Excellent facilitation and stakeholder management skills; comfortable driving alignment, negotiating trade-offs, and presenting clear recommendations to senior leaders.
Fluency across delivery methodologies and tools (Agile, Scrum, Kanban, Waterfall) with sound judgment to apply the right approach per initiative.
High adaptability and structured problem-solving in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
Strong technical fluency across modern platforms and digital tools, enabling effective partnership with architecture and engineering teams.
Demonstrated prior experience as a champion for AI fluency and adoption of agentic capabilities, including identifying and delivering tools and opportunities to embed AI-assisted workflows into program execution (e.g., portfolio insights, delivery automation, risk identification, stakeholder communications) in partnership with product, engineering, and control stakeholders.
AI fluency and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to evaluate and apply agentic tools to improve delivery execution and transparency while balancing governance and risk.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

Experience supporting programs spanning HR and Technology / employee platforms.
Certifications (Agile/Scrum, PMP, Lean, Prosci/change management)

About Us

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. jobs.description:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Project Manager - Enterprise Merchandise

As a Project Manager, you will be the operational backbone of our enterprise sales process. You will partner directly with Account Executives to manage the complete order-to-delivery lifecycle for clients, ensuring flawless execution and exceptional customer experience. Working alongside the sales team, you will leverage deep product knowledge and operational excellence to support deal closure and drive client satisfaction. Your role is critical to scaling our enterprise business while maintaining the quality and attention to detail that defines Quince.

Responsibilities

Assume deal ownership post-sale, from logo approval through invoicing, delivery and issue resolution
Track and update all project progress in our B2B operations tracker, sharing timely updates with clients and Account Executives; communicate with clarity even when information is incomplete or ambiguous
Finalize customization details, communicate delivery timelines, and manage approval workflows with clients and internal teams
Field and resolve client support requests including sample returns, shipping and tracking, troubleshooting missing or damaged items, and expediting requests when possible
Demonstrate strategic thinking by proactively identifying opportunities to streamline operations, reduce tasks, and propose solutions that enhance client experience
Over-communicate with customers on all issues, managing them with confidence and compassion; reply to requests with urgency and follow through on every commitment made

Qualifications

Required:

1+ years of experience in project management, operations, or vendor management
Familiarity with CRM or project management platforms to track client data, order status, and communication history (Hubspot preferred)
Proficiency in Google Workspace
Experience managing internal and external stakeholders with distinct approaches
Self-starter comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
Extremely detail-oriented with ability to operate with a sense of urgency
Customer service oriented and customer obsessed—committed to exceeding expectations at every touchpoint

Preferred:

Customer experience or customer-facing background (email-based support, retail customer service, or account coordination)
Exposure to apparel, decoration, manufacturing, or promotional products industry

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Pay Range: $62,500 USD - $75,000 USD

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

jobs.description:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Project Manager - Enterprise Merchandise

As a Project Manager, you will be the operational backbone of our enterprise sales process. You will partner directly with Account Executives to manage the complete order-to-delivery lifecycle for clients, ensuring flawless execution and exceptional customer experience. Working alongside the sales team, you will leverage deep product knowledge and operational excellence to support deal closure and drive client satisfaction. Your role is critical to scaling our enterprise business while maintaining the quality and attention to detail that defines Quince.

Responsibilities

Assume deal ownership post-sale, from logo approval through invoicing, delivery and issue resolution
Track and update all project progress in our B2B operations tracker, sharing timely updates with clients and Account Executives; communicate with clarity even when information is incomplete or ambiguous
Finalize customization details, communicate delivery timelines, and manage approval workflows with clients and internal teams
Field and resolve client support requests including sample returns, shipping and tracking, troubleshooting missing or damaged items, and expediting requests when possible
Demonstrate strategic thinking by proactively identifying opportunities to streamline operations, reduce tasks, and propose solutions that enhance client experience
Over-communicate with customers on all issues, managing them with confidence and compassion; reply to requests with urgency and follow through on every commitment made

Qualifications

Required:

1+ years of experience in project management, operations, or vendor management
Familiarity with CRM or project management platforms to track client data, order status, and communication history (Hubspot preferred)
Proficiency in Google Workspace
Experience managing internal and external stakeholders with distinct approaches
Self-starter comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
Extremely detail-oriented with ability to operate with a sense of urgency
Customer service oriented and customer obsessed—committed to exceeding expectations at every touchpoint

Preferred:

Customer experience or customer-facing background (email-based support, retail customer service, or account coordination)
Exposure to apparel, decoration, manufacturing, or promotional products industry

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Pay Range: $62,500 USD - $75,000 USD

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager (AI Delivery)
jobs.description:
Location: Remote, United States or Canada.
Core hours: 8 AM to 5 PM US Eastern, weekdays.
Type: Full time.
Compensation: Up to $150,000 USD base, depending on experience. Eligible for bonus and additional compensation after year one.
Works with: our CEO, our COO, our Full Stack Agentic Developer, and each client's project team, IT lead and executive sponsor.
Start date: Immediate.

About Brainverse

Brainverse builds custom AI agent solutions for businesses, from small companies to enterprises near $1 billion in revenue. Some run on IP we own. Others are built from scratch for one client, such as an agent team that runs part of their operations inside their own environment.

We run our own company the same way: more than 100 agents work across our sales, marketing, delivery and engineering every day. Our signed work is growing faster than our team, and this role owns client delivery.

The role

You run client projects from signed scope to go-live, and you are the client's main point of contact for the life of the project.

Projects arrive with a signed scope, an architecture and an initial design. Your job is the thousand details between that design and a working system in the client's environment: you find the open questions, get the answers, turn them into requirements the developer can build from, and keep every date honest.

This is a technical role without production code. You will be in technical conversations every day: with a client's IT team about their cloud, identity and security review; with our developer about what is ready; and with the AI agents we use to plan, track and draft.

What you'll do

Fill in the details:

Take the signed scope and design and work out everything the build still needs to know: data sources, user roles, integrations, edge cases, environment and security constraints.

Ask the client the questions that close each gap, before the build reaches it.

Turn the answers into requirements and acceptance criteria clear enough to build and test from.

Run the project

Turn the scope into a plan with milestones, owners, dependencies and dates.

Run the weekly client sync, send a written update after each one, and keep a running log of decisions and open questions.

Chase answers on both sides. When a date is going to slip, you know first and bring a plan.

Manage scope. A new request mid-project gets documented, sized with the developer, and approved as a change before anyone builds it.

Get it running in the client's environment

Work with the client's IT team on everything a deployment needs: cloud access, identity and single sign-on, network and firewall rules, hosting, data access and security review.

Own the IT prerequisites list for each project and drive it to done. Clients run on Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, on-premises servers and a wide mix of business systems.

Coordinate cutover and go-live so the client's people know what changes and when.

Keep the work visible and true

Keep the task board current every day: every task has an owner and a date, and overdue work gets a new date or gets raised.

Test what comes back against the requirements before the client sees it.

Acknowledge client support requests during the project the same business day, route technical issues to the right person, and confirm when they're closed.

Make delivery repeatable

Write and improve our delivery playbooks: kickoff, IT prerequisites, weekly sync, go-live and handoff.

Build the systems and agent workflows that make the next project faster than the last.

Not part of this role

Winning new clients or growing existing accounts. That stays with leadership.

Writing production code or designing the architecture.

What we're looking for

Must have

5 or more years delivering business software into customer environments, as an implementation manager, technical project manager, solutions or deployment engineer, or technical account manager.

You have run several client projects at once, start to finish, with real dates and real accountability.

You know how software gets deployed and secured inside a company: cloud and on-premises hosting, identity and single sign-on, permissions, networking basics, and what an IT security review asks for.

You turn a messy client conversation into a clear written list of what is decided, what is open, and who owes what by when.

Excellent communication in fluent English: written, on video calls, and in person when a client needs it. You are as clear with a client's IT lead as with their executive sponsor.

You use AI tools daily to plan, draft, summarize and analyze real work, and can show us how.

You notice what is about to slip before anyone else does, and you act on it without being asked.

You want a fast, demanding startup pace. Hours aren't fixed. Communication seven days a week is expected; working seven days a week is not.

Work samples (plans, requirements, status reports or playbooks, with confidential details removed).

Nice to have

Experience growing client accounts through relationships across an organization.

PMP, Scrum or a similar certification.

Hands-on administration of Azure, AWS, Google Cloud or Microsoft 365.

Experience with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.

Background in construction, mechanical or electrical contracting, or construction software.

Experience at an early-stage company or a consulting firm.

What success looks like

30 days: You've joined every live client project and know each client by name, status and next milestone.

60 days: You lead at least one client project, and the task board reflects reality every day without anyone asking.

90 days: You run several projects with leadership out of the day-to-day, the first delivery playbooks exist, and clients call you first.

How we hire

Intro call. 30 minutes on your background and what you want next.
Client simulation. You get a project briefing a day ahead. Then, in a one-hour call, our team plays the client's leadership and IT team, and you run the conversation.
Conversation with our CEO.
Reference checks.

You don't send references when you apply. We'll ask for them before the reference checks.

ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

Lead stakeholder communications, training coordination, adoption planning, and organizational change activities across affected departments and locations.
Coordinate procurement and vendor activities, including deliverables, schedules, dependencies, performance, and issue escalation.
Facilitate cross-functional workshops, working sessions, readiness reviews, and post-migration retrospectives.

Certification of Capability in Business Analysis (CCBA) or Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP).
Working knowledge of ITIL practices.
Experience with enterprise cloud storage migrations, application migrations, infrastructure modernization, or related security and compliance requirements.

Position Purpose

The Project Manager Senior is responsible for simultaneously directing the efforts of multiple cross-functional project teams to achieve clearly defined results within the triple constraints of time, budget and specifications for medium and high-complexity projects. This position is responsible for an average of 3-6 projects as well as low-complexity programs. The position is responsible for assembling the project team, developing the project work plan, and managing the expectations, deliverables and results of all internal and external project resources for the roles and activities defined in the plan. This includes managing outside vendors to ensure they meet contractual deliverables. The Project Manager is responsible for tracking project milestones and making necessary adjustments to the project plan or resources to maintain customer commitments. The Project Manager communicates project status and risks to all project stakeholders via standardized project status reports and manages the change process for each assigned project.

Major Tasks, Responsibilities, And Key Accountabilities

Manages three or more medium- to large-scale projects from planning to completion by facilitating meetings with project stakeholders. Develops, analyzes, and manages project estimation and execution plans, schedules, and resource forecasts. Manages project financials and provides input and justification for costs and budget impacts. Monitors overall project performance against plan and makes adjustments as needed. Identifies and resolves issues. Provides insight and direction for the request for information and vendor request for proposal processes.
Manages the work of multiple project teams by recommending or requesting resources based on the alignment of team member skills and project demands. Communicates a clear vision of project goals and objectives to the team. Coordinates team activities to ensure project milestones are achieved. Lead and provide work direction to a project team to determine project scope, devise and maintain a workable plan, and to develop and deploy the solution in accordance with the needs of the project. Provides performance feedback to team members as needed.
Manages, controls, and mitigates risks across multiple projects by analyzing and identifying trigger events. Manage the project change control process, status reporting, project estimating, monthly cost accounting and vendor invoice processing. Establishes contingency plans, anticipates and manages dependencies affected by ongoing changes across projects, and recommends ways to mitigate future risks. Influences management to take action on these recommendations.
Manages the alignment, buy-in, and support of diverse project stakeholders by building and maintaining relationships with internal customers, third party vendors, and senior management. Manage interaction between the customer, vendors, and the internal project team to ensure that appropriate relationships exist to produce positive project outcomes. Provides insight and recommendations to Program Managers to drive the development of project goals, influence the prioritization of deliverables, and facilitate decisions necessary for project delivery.
Adheres to enterprise project management practices by participating in formal and informal training sessions. Tracks and reports key metrics as needed. Gathers, maintains, and communicates lessons learned and feedback to team members, management, and the larger project management community.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification
6+ years of project management experience, including 8+ years of IT or related business experience.
3 to 5 years of experience working on projects involving the implementation of project life cycle methodologies.
Experience influencing and managing project teams without formal direct reporting relationships.
Experience managing SDLC projects using an iterative methodology preferred.
Comprehensive knowledge of PMI based project management competency areas and methodologies and experience applying these methods to manage successful projects.
Analytical skills are required to effectively manage activities related to budgeting, forecasting, monitoring, process management, risk management, quality control and reporting.
Strong oral and written communication skills and experience leveraging these skills to interact with all levels of management.
Strong negotiation and influencing skills.
High-level understanding of IT infrastructure and application architectures desired.
High-level of proficiency in Microsoft Office products, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Visio, and Project.
High-level of proficiency using Microsoft SharePoint.

Typically requires BS/BA in a related discipline. Generally 8+ years of experience in a related field OR MS/MA and generally 5+ years of experience in a related field. Certification is required in some areas.

Displays the highest level of critical thinking and analysis in bringing successful resolution to high-impact, complex, and/or cross-departmental problems. Makes prompt, sound decisions when faced with complex and often contradictory alternatives that result in successful outcomes.

Autonomy

Operates with considerable latitude. Situations may have little or no precedent requiring original or new concepts or approaches without guidance from others. Reaches decisions under conditions of uncertainty.

Leadership

Develops or engages/directs others in developing innovative solutions to important, highly complex strategic and operating problems; cross-departmental considerations are often present.

Most of the time is spent sitting in a comfortable position and there is frequent opportunity to move about. On rare occasions there may be a need to move or lift light articles.

Come join us in accelerating the energy and infrastructure transition!
Basic Function

As a member of the Data Center Supply Chain team, the Senior Program Manager, Logistics Control Tower & Analytics will own supplier logistics readiness and run the dedicated Control Tower provider/team supporting domestic OFCI execution. The role maintains live portfolio data, daily operating reviews, exceptions and action closure, performance reporting and business requirements for logistics tools. The Control Tower coordinates their readiness and agreed handoff evidence. The shared Supply Chain Governance and Assurance function owns the common framework; IT owns technical delivery and service.
SB Energy is building a procurement team under a common role profile, bringing together complementary electrical, mechanical, commercial, and logistics strengths. Within this team, this role focuses on logistics control tower operations, including shipment and milestone visibility, data quality, exception management, and performance reporting. The manager may lead control tower activities for an individual project, manage logistics visibility and reporting across multiple projects, or lead a shared logistics analytics or process improvement assignment.
Assignments may evolve as projects advance, workloads shift, and business priorities change. The manager is expected to contribute beyond their primary area, including broader procurement, sourcing, supplier development, or planning assignments, based on relevant experience, equipment knowledge, readiness, workload, and appropriate specialist support. Each manager maintains clear ownership of assigned responsibilities, cross-trains colleagues, and provides structured handoffs and backup coverage.
Candidates must demonstrate depth in logistics control tower operations, data analysis, and exception management, together with the flexibility and willingness to build capability across the broader function. Candidates are not expected to be specialists in every electrical, mechanical, commercial, or logistics discipline.

Responsibilities

Portfolio and Supplier Readiness:
Maintain one reconciled OFCI register linking projects, equipment, POs, OEM readiness, agreed handoffs, domestic shipments, storage, custody, costs and exceptions. Track shipping-data completeness, cargo-ready commitments, packaging/preservation evidence and open readiness actions with OEMs. Procurement retains manufacturing/commercial expediting; Engineering/Quality retains technical release. Preserve required/baseline, planned, forecast, committed and actual dates and the data date.
Daily Operating Reviews:
Direct the dedicated Control Tower team’s daily readiness, exception and action-closure work. Make risks to Required on Site Dates visible, secure accountable owners and escalate recovery decisions. Transportation authorizes domestic dispatch; Storage/Site owns inventory and preservation controls; designated functions retain their approvals.
Decision and Delivery Tracking:
Maintain operating decision, action, risk, dependency, and change logs. Track the implementation plan across staffing, providers, contracts, processes, data, and training. Escalate overdue decisions, unassigned work, and resource gaps with a recommendation and decision deadline.
Business Product Ownership:
Define operating requirements, prioritize the backlog, and lead user acceptance testing and adoption for the OFCI Logistics Control Hub or approved equivalent. Start with available tools and practical controls; agree build, release, support, and service ownership with designated Analytics and IT teams.
Data and Reporting:
Define logistics KPI logic, source lineage, data-quality checks, dashboards, and executive decision views with capability owners and Finance. Reconcile incomplete or conflicting records, assign corrections to source owners, and keep material uncertainty visible. Validate technical deliverables against business requirements.
Provider Performance:
Own the dedicated Control Tower provider/team’s scope, staffing, coverage, service levels, data quality, operational reviews and corrective actions. Require OEM-readiness and end-to-end logistics experience, evidence access and export rights. Support transport and warehouse leads with common reporting; their respective providers retain contracted execution obligations.
Governance and Assurance Interface:
Apply common process, documentation, control, and evidence standards set with the shared Supply Chain Governance and Assurance function. Supply authoritative OFCI records for its reviews, coordinate operational corrective actions, and escalate recurring control weaknesses without creating duplicate trackers.
Adoption and Improvement:
Lead OFCI-specific user guidance, training, release communications, and workflow improvements. Coordinate changes to common standards with Governance and Assurance and obtain functional approval for release-criteria changes. Prioritize automation against data readiness, approved technical design, and funded capacity.

Qualifications/Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, logistics, business, engineering, information systems, construction management, analytics, or a related field.
At least 10 years of relevant experience, including at least 5 years leading complex cross-functional programs, logistics control towers, or operating-model implementation in supply chain, infrastructure, construction, manufacturing, or a comparable environment.
Demonstrated experience leading supplier logistics readiness and a dedicated Control Tower team, with milestone models, readiness gates, exception resolution, action closure and operating reviews that improve execution.
Hands-on ability to structure and reconcile operational data in Excel or comparable tools, define KPIs and data-quality controls, and turn incomplete information into useful decision views.
Experience translating business needs into requirements, prioritized backlogs, acceptance criteria, user testing, deployment, and adoption with analysts and IT.
Strong executive writing, facilitation, and matrix leadership; ability to secure clear ownership and drive action while live operations continue.

Preferred Qualifications

Data center, cloud infrastructure, power, energy, EPC, industrial, or comparable large capital-program experience.
Experience with logistics platforms, provider data, Power BI, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Power Platform, or comparable analytics and workflow tools.
Experience with provider-team mobilization and performance, OEM readiness and handoff control, cost/benefits tracking and change adoption; relevant program-management or product-owner certification.

Working arrangements
Assignments may span projects, equipment categories, suppliers, and locations and may change with business needs. The role includes supplier, factory, warehouse, and active construction site visits, coordination across time zones, and compliance with site safety and access requirements. Managers lead execution through qualified suppliers and project resources.  
Location: 
Redwood City, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Austin, TX
US remote locations considered on a case by case basis.
This role leads programs and business product delivery across distributed teams, providers, and time zones, with visits to project sites and implementation sessions. Designated technical teams own application engineering, integrations, architecture, security, administration, and ongoing technical service.

About The Role

Notion is looking for a Recruiting Program Manager to help design, build, and scale the systems and programs that power how we hire. This is a role for someone who moves fast, takes ownership, and doesn't wait to be told what to do — someone who operates with both strategic altitude and operational precision, and knows how to bring clarity and momentum to complex cross-functional work.

You'll partner closely with Recruiters, Recruiting Operations, People Operations, and senior leadership to drive some of our highest-priority initiatives — building the programs and processes that define how Notion finds, evaluates, and brings in exceptional talent.

The Life Sciences Program Executive (PE) is a senior, executive-facing individual contributor (IC) within the Global Life Sciences Acceleration Hub at Salesforce. The ideal candidate brings a deep background in Life Sciences (pharma, biotech, medtech, or related sectors) combined with IT or management consulting delivery experience, leveraging that industry credibility as a strategic advisor to customers, partners, and internal teams across Salesforce.

Life Sciences Program Executives sit at the helm of AI and Agentforce transformations that accelerate drug commercialization, streamline field engagement, and modernize clinical and commercial operations through intelligent, autonomous agents. They lead cross-functional teams deploying digital workforces that bridge the gap between complex Life Sciences data and actionable business outcomes, driving the next frontier of Life Sciences innovation.

Their success is defined by what they deliver, what they prevent, and the customer confidence they command.

AI and agentic delivery are embedded in how you work: you actively leverage AI tooling and agentic workflows to optimize how your program teams deliver. You reduce manual overhead, accelerate insight, and model the productivity gains Life Sciences customers are investing in Salesforce to achieve.

Value delivered translates into real adoption and consumption: you drive the transformational changes, especially around AI and agentic capabilities, needed to achieve customers' objectives, informed by deep Life Sciences industry and product expertise. Risk is managed before it manages you: you anticipate, mitigate, and manage risk to Salesforce and the customer, taking decisive program action to address risk profiles. You raise signals with a recommended path, not just a problem statement. Surfacing a risk is success; being surprised by one is not.

SAP Project Manager (PM)
SAP Project Manager (PM) is responsible for providing support to the IT group and overseeing the implementation of SAP projects. You must work closely with stakeholders, including the executive team, department managers, IT personnel, and end-users, to ensure the SAP applications (ECC, S4HANA, GRC, etc.) meet the organization’s requirements and objectives. You will play a major part in the successful implementation of the SAP applications helping it to remain within budget, on schedule, and to the satisfaction of stakeholders.
What you will do

Regulations & Standards: The PM must ensure that the project is compliant with all relevant SOX regulations and Change Management and Project Management policies.
Delivery: The PM is responsible for providing support to the Delivery team, including scheduling meetings, organizing community events, formatting, maintaining issue logs and risk registers, taking minutes, and reporting. They must ensure all information and documentation is processed, maintained, monitored, and filed.
Planning and Management: The PM is responsible for creating and maintaining a comprehensive project plan that outlines the project’s scope, schedule, budget, and resources required. They must also work with the project team to agree roles and responsibilities and create a communication plan that includes regular status updates and stakeholder engagement. The PM should monitor progress, identify risks, and develop mitigation strategies to keep the project on track.
Stakeholder Management: The PM must work closely with stakeholders, including the executive team, department managers, IT personnel, and end-users, to ensure the SAP applications meet the organization’s requirements and objectives. They must develop and maintain relationships with stakeholders, communicate project updates, and manage expectations to ensure stakeholder satisfaction.
Budget Management: The PM must establish a project budget, track costs, and report on budget variances. They must work with stakeholders to identify cost-saving opportunities and develop contingency plans to manage project costs effectively.
Risk Management: The PM must identify project risks and develop contingency plans to mitigate these risks. They should be proactive in identifying risks and work with stakeholders to develop a risk management plan that includes risk assessment, risk response, and risk monitoring.
Resource Management: The PM must manage project resources, including project team members, vendors, and contractors. They must ensure that the project team is appropriately staffed, trained, and motivated to achieve project objectives.

What we are looking for

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, computer science, or a related field.

new_jobs.title: Protective Intelligence Analyst- OSINT Monitoring and Triage
new_jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly capable Protective Intelligence Analyst to support the protection of senior Vanguard executives globally. This role requires an experienced OSINT practitioner who can independently manage threat identification and triage, prioritize competing executive protection needs, and produce decision-ready intelligence products under time pressure. The position owns the threat identification and initial assessment function for Vanguard’s protective intelligence program, including the daily monitoring and alert queue through which every inbound threat communication, platform alert, and referral receives its initial assessment. The Protective Intelligence Analyst will distinguish credible concerns from noise, open cases for identified security concerns, and manage case tracking and related metrics for the program. The role offers broad exposure across the protective intelligence lifecycle and meaningful ownership of threat intake, applying structured analytic judgment to determine which matters warrant escalation or further investigation.

Monitoring & Triage

Manage daily alert and intake queues: vendor alerting feeds, the program’s intake channels, executive-assistant and partner referrals, and regional intelligence routing.
Triage inbound items against the program’s established threat screening criteria; disposition items as unfounded with documented rationale or open cases for investigation.
Provide dedicated monitoring coverage during executive travel and event windows, assessing emerging developments in real time and escalating per defined criteria.
Maintain watchlist hygiene and help fine tune OSINT feeds to ensure reliable threat identification.

Case Management & Intelligence Production

Maintain key protective intelligence trackers/metrics: request log, alert log, case entries, product IDs, and dashboard integrity.
Conduct OSINT collection and analysis for protective intelligence assessments, documenting sources and findings and contributing analytic judgments to final products.
Draft the program’s weekly intelligence summary, synthesizing alert activity, case developments, and emerging threat trends into concise, decision-ready reporting.
Process intake acknowledgements and maintain records-handling standards for intake channels.

Team Model – Primary Focus, Universal Capability

Triage and monitoring is the primary focus of this role, not an exclusive lane. Every Protective Intelligence Analyst trains to produce the program’s core assessment products to standard, rotates through triage and monitoring coverage, and serves as designated backup for at least one other product line, so the team carries no single points of failure.
Cross-train teammates in triage and monitoring, maintain current proficiency in teammates’ specialties, and participate in the program’s dual-review and after-action practices.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security studies, psychology, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
Minimum of three years of related experience in a field such as intelligence analysis, GSOC/watch operations, journalism/research, or military/law-enforcement analysis.
Demonstrated ability to work a high-volume queue with consistency, accuracy, and documented decisions.
Strong OSINT skills, including the ability to locate, verify, and assess the credibility of information across open sources.
Comfort with reading concerning or threatening content professionally and escalating appropriately.
High ethical standards and discretion when handling sensitive executive and corporate information.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders clearly and calmly under time pressure.
Proven ability to think critically and assess incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting information.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with threat intelligence, alerting, or case management platforms.
Formal training or applied experience in threat assessment, targeted violence prevention, or intelligence analysis.
ATAP membership, with active interest or progress toward obtaining the Certified Threat Manager (CTM) designation.

Special Factors

Participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours escalation support as the program matures.
Early-morning queue coverage; occasional evening and weekend surge coverage during executive travel windows.
Occasional domestic travel (

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

new_jobs.title: Competitive Intelligence Analyst, Oncology Diagnosis (Hybrid)
new_jobs.description:
At Caris, we understand that cancer is an ugly word—a word no one wants to hear, but one that connects us all. That’s why we’re not just transforming cancer care—we’re changing lives.

We introduced precision medicine to the world and built an industry around the idea that every patient deserves answers as unique as their DNA. Backed by cutting-edge molecular science and AI, we ask ourselves every day: “What would I do if this patient were my mom?” That question drives everything we do.

But our mission doesn’t stop with cancer. We're pushing the frontiers of medicine and leading a revolution in healthcare—driven by innovation, compassion, and purpose.

Join us in our mission to improve the human condition across multiple diseases. If you're passionate about meaningful work and want to be part of something bigger than yourself, Caris is where your impact begins.

Position Summary

Generate actionable intelligence on the scientific, clinical, and competitive landscape for next-generation sequencing (NGS) and other molecular diagnostic tests used in oncology.
Apply scientific and clinical oncology expertise or in-depth oncology diagnostics market analysis experience to interpret evidence, assess product differentiation, and inform decisions across Commercial, Marketing, Medical Affairs, and R&D.

Job Responsibilities

Scientific and Clinical Analysis

Critically evaluate publications, clinical trials, validation studies, and congress presentations to assess assay performance, clinical validity, clinical utility, and relevance to patient care.
Analyze developments in comprehensive genomic profiling, tissue and liquid biopsy, companion diagnostics, molecular residual disease testing, and emerging early detection approaches.
Compare study designs, patient populations, endpoints, and methodological limitations to determine the strength of evidence supporting diagnostic claims.
Monitor oncology testing guidelines and clinical practice developments that may affect test adoption, evidence requirements, or product positioning.

Market and Competitive Landscape Analysis

Track competitor test launches, product enhancements, regulatory activity, partnerships, pricing, reimbursement, and commercial developments.
Develop competitor and product profiles that compare test capabilities, clinical applications, supporting evidence, sample requirements, turnaround times, and workflow considerations.
Conduct focused market assessments and primary and secondary research to identify competitive threats, unmet needs, and opportunities for differentiation.
Produce monthly intelligence updates, quarterly landscape reviews, dashboards, and targeted analyses that explain the implications of scientific and market developments.

Strategic Insights and Collaboration

Translate complex scientific and business information into clear conclusions and practical recommendations for functional leaders.
Partner with Medical Affairs, R&D, Commercial, and Marketing to assess emerging evidence and support positioning, evidence generation, and launch planning.
Collaborate with Market Access and Business Development on payer coverage trends, reimbursement developments, partnership evaluations, and opportunity assessments.
Support intelligence planning, coverage, and debriefs for major oncology and molecular diagnostics congresses, including ASCO, ESMO, and AMP.

Tools and Processes

Use scientific databases, regulatory resources, market research, analyst reports, and expert interviews to build well-supported intelligence deliverables.
Apply AI tools to improve research and synthesis while verifying source accuracy and protecting confidential information.
Maintain a searchable intelligence repository with clear sourcing, consistent updates, and accessible reporting formats.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in life sciences, molecular biology, genetics, or a related field.
At least 3 years of relevant experience demonstrating depth through either of the following pathways:

Scientific or clinical experience in oncology and oncology diagnostics, including molecular pathology, tumor genomics, translational research, clinical research, or medical affairs, with demonstrated ability to assess diagnostic evidence and its strategic implications.
Substantial experience focused on oncology diagnostics market analysis, competitive intelligence, equity research, consulting, or a related analyst role, with demonstrated ability to interpret scientific and clinical evidence.
Strong understanding of cancer biology, molecular diagnostic technologies, and the role of testing in treatment selection and disease monitoring.
Ability to critically assess clinical and technical evidence and distinguish established findings from preliminary results and promotional claims.
Experience integrating publications, clinical trial data, company disclosures, market research, and expert input into clear, defensible conclusions.
Strong analytical, writing, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate with scientific and commercial audiences.
Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, scientific literature searching, and relevant research or data visualization tools.
Ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize deadlines, and work independently with high integrity and appropriate handling of confidential information.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or clinical discipline, such as an MS, PhD, MD, PharmD or equivalent; an MBA with substantial oncology diagnostics experience is also valuable.
Experience in a molecular diagnostics laboratory, oncology diagnostics company, or research or advisory organization focused on precision oncology.
Familiarity with diagnostic regulatory pathways, payer coverage, reimbursement, and commercial adoption drivers.
Experience conducting expert interviews or developing scientific and competitive congress summaries.

Physical Demands

Ability to travel, including occasional evenings and weekends, as required for congresses and business needs.
Ability to perform typical office activities, including using standard office equipment and handling routine office supplies.

Training

Complete all job-specific, safety, and compliance training assigned based on the responsibilities of the role.

Conditions of Employment:
Individual must successfully complete pre-employment process, which includes criminal background check, drug screening, credit check ( applicable for certain positions) and reference verification.

This job description reflects management’s assignment of essential functions. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.
